translationRepairs: During the Zhenguan reign he was made Commandant of the Horse Stables for Imperial Sons-in-Law and married Princess Taogu of the Shenyao line.
During the Zhenguan reign he was made Commandant of the Horse Stables for Imperial Sons-in-Law and married Princess Guantao of the Shenyao line.

Focus unit 尚神堯館陶公主 names 館陶 (Guantao), not Taogu; the idiomatic English reverses the characters. The proposed replacement restores the correct princess title while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.
In the Zhenguan era he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Stables for Imperial Sons-in-Law and married Princess Taogu of the Shenyao lineage.
In the Zhenguan era he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Stables for Imperial Sons-in-Law and married Princess Guantao of the Shenyao lineage.
The same focus unit has 館陶公主; reading it as Taogu reverses 館 and 陶. Guantao is the accurate rendering, matching the Chinese and the corrected idiomatic.
When Suzong reached Lingbow, halls and imperial screens all imitated the palace; each prince and princess had a separate courtyard; food sent to the throne exhausted land and water delicacies.
When Suzong reached Lingwu, halls and imperial screens all imitated the palace; each prince and princess had a separate courtyard; food sent to the throne exhausted land and water delicacies.
Focus unit 肅宗至靈武 is Lingwu; neighboring units also use 靈武 as Lingwu. "Lingbow" is a corrupted transliteration with no support in the Chinese.
